application_alignment: The application proposal targets single-image full-head modeling by replacing PanoHead's NeRF rendering with Gaussian representation, using diffusion only as an audited prior for invisible regions, using Transformer-style consistency, and anchoring geometry with FLAME/FaceVerse/3DMM.
authorized_next_experiments: G40a: optional local-only LAM smoke on one Multiface train view; record command, hashes, timing, and manual/VLM notes only; no identifiable media sync.
G40b: repo-safe LAM smoke on the CC0 synthetic positive-control front view; sync MP4/PNG/JSON/MD, but label it positive-control only.
G41: design a true head-anchored Gaussian scaffold/adapter that can render held-out cameras or export mesh/point-cloud for GT metrics before any quality claim.
blocked_actions: Do not train or evaluate reconstruction quality on experiments/downstream_datasets.
Do not use Multiface GT mesh as input to a single-image method; it is evaluation geometry only.
Do not publish identifiable Multiface RGB, generated avatar videos, meshes, or textured assets without artifact/privacy review.
Do not claim learned-prior quality from LAM videos alone; require held-out camera-aligned metrics or geometry metrics.
Do not restart longer RI3D training from G33 as a method milestone.

case_summary.privacy_status: recognizable human-subject dataset; public repo export limited to metadata/hashes unless artifact review approves derived contact sheets
case_summary.repo_policy: local benchmark case; commit compact metrics, hashes, and gate reports only unless user explicitly approves identifiable derived PNG export

decision: Open G40 only as gated learned-prior smoke/positive-control work. The real-GT/data/VLM premise is satisfied locally, but model-quality claims remain blocked until a head-anchored method produces held-out camera-aligned renders or GT geometry metrics.
distribution_statement: LAM-20K is documented as trained on VFHQ + NeRSemble. The current real-GT case is Multiface: a nearby multi-view head-capture domain but not proven in-distribution for the released LAM weights. Therefore LAM-on-Multiface can be interpreted only as local qualitative or plumbing evidence unless we obtain camera-aligned render/geometry outputs and compare against held-out views/GT geometry.

literature_anchors.signal: Single-forward-pass Gaussian head; FLAME canonical points query Transformer image features.
One-shot full-head Gaussian synthesis; FLAME sparse points plus transformer, synthetic 3D-GAN priors.
Single-image drivable Gaussian head avatar with FLAME-based hierarchical UV Gaussian splatting.
Feed-forward 360 full-head animatable Gaussian avatar with semantic-aware mesh deformation and UV fusion.
Structured Plucker-aware Gaussian scaffold and one-step conditional denoising for single-image full-head reconstruction.
Feed-forward one-shot animatable mesh head; useful successor signal for topology and texture anchoring.
Few-shot feed-forward Gaussian head reconstruction with multi-view fusion, FLAME prediction, and NeRSemble metrics.

method_positioning.implication: Use only as a baseline/smoke until camera-aligned held-out rendering or geometry export is available; LAM uses FLAME canonical points as Transformer queries for Gaussian attributes.
They define the correct scientific direction: feed-forward full-head priors, FLAME/UV or structured Gaussian scaffolds, dense multi-view supervision, and benchmark metrics.
Keep as diagnostic evidence only; do not scale training without a new method premise.
May inform failure taxonomy or conditional priors after VLM audit, never GT training views.

premise: The next credible method route is learned-prior / feed-forward / head-anchored Gaussian head reconstruction, not longer RI3D optimization over pseudo-view candidates.
